title: ICMR completes 100 technology transfer deals in under two years
summary: The milestone was announced at the 3rd DHR-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit, where 20 licensing agreements covering eight technologies were exchanged with nine Indian companies

contentHtml:
The milestone was announced at the 3rd DHR-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit, where 20 licensing agreements covering eight technologies were exchanged with nine Indian companies

The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has completed 100 technology transfer deals, marking a milestone in translating indigenous health research into technologies and solutions for public use. The announcement was made at the 3rd Department of Health Research (DHR)-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit, which concluded on November 17, 2026, at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.

Organised by DHR and ICMR on November 16 and 17, 2026, the two-day Summit brought together over 600 scientists, researchers, innovators, administrators and policymakers from ICMR institutes, partner institutions, government organisations and academia. The Summit also marked 115 years of ICMR’s contribution to biomedical and health research in the country.

The Summit serves as a national platform for recognising contributions to health research and promoting the translation of scientific evidence into outcomes. It showcases contributions from ICMR institutes and extramural partner institutions across research publications, technologies, patents and research management, while facilitating collaboration among researchers, industry and policymakers.

At the Technology Transfer Ceremony, ICMR exchanged 20 licensing agreements covering eight technologies with nine Indian companies. This took the cumulative number of successful technology transfer deals to 100 in less than two years of Medical Innovations Patent Mitra, an ICMR initiative launched by Union Health and Family Welfare Minister J P Nadda in March 2025. The milestone reflects ICMR’s efforts to facilitate the translation of research and indigenous innovations into applications through industry partnerships.

An Innovation Exhibition showcased 17 technologies developed by ICMR institutes and extramural partner institutions. In addition, 10 technologies and eight patents were presented during a session on Technologies and Patents.

Three initiatives were launched at the Summit. DHR’s Research to Action Vertical will translate research evidence into decision-ready products for policy and programmes. Syndromic Surveillance under the DHR Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDL) Scheme will create an early-warning network for outbreaks across 70 VRDLs and Infectious Disease Research & Diagnostic Laboratories (IRDLs). The Dr M K Bhan Young Medical Faculty PhD Portal will serve as a centralised digital platform providing information for prospective applicants.

ICMR also released the Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) Annual Report and Standard Operating Procedures, bringing together the national evidence base on antimicrobial resistance and laboratory procedures. The ICMR Compendium, featuring 25 stories of research translated into outcomes for people, was also released.

The Research Excellence Showcase presented shortlisted publications, while the Innovation Excellence Showcase featured shortlisted technologies and patents. A track on research administration and finance discussed measures to streamline grant management, procurement and financial processes. A session also commemorated the Golden Jubilee of the ICMR-National Institute of Malaria Research (ICMR-NIMR), marking 50 years of its contribution to malaria research.

The Summit recognised contributions across the health research ecosystem through the Research, Innovation and Institutional Excellence Recognition. Researchers and institutions were recognised across nine categories for achievements in publications, technologies, patents and institutional performance.

The ICMR Research Management Excellence Recognition acknowledged the contributions of reviewers involved in project selection, the Indian Journal of Medical Research, scientific divisions, scientific support units, and administration and finance teams in strengthening the research ecosystem and supporting research.

The top 100 school students selected through the SHINE National Competition were also recognised at the Summit for their contributions and scientific thinking in public health. SHINE (Science and Health Innovation for the NextGen Explorers) is an ICMR initiative for students in Grades 9 to 12 from government, government-aided and private schools across the country. The initiative seeks to foster scientific temper, encourage curiosity and inspire students to explore careers in biomedical and health research.

The Summit reaffirmed the importance of a collaborative and innovation-driven health research ecosystem in addressing national health priorities and advancing India’s pursuit of accessible, affordable and quality healthcare.

Headquartered in New Delhi, the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) is India’s apex body for the formulation, coordination and promotion of biomedical research. Established in 1911, ICMR functions under the Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India.
